exposure: Ultrasound Doppler parameters (fetal vessels, flow patterns in aortic isthmus and ductus venosus, umbilical artery pulsatility and resistive indices)
outcome: poor fetal outcomes (APGAR score, neonatal death, neonatal complications including respiratory distress syndrome, sepsis, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, intracerebral and intraventricular haemorrhage, duration of NICU stay, birth weight)
cohort: 65 high-risk pregnant mothers, predominantly aged 23-27 years, with risk factors like gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, and anaemia.
finding: Increased pulsatility and resistive indices in umbilical arteries, as well as flow reversal in the aortic isthmus and ductus venosus, were significantly associated with poor perinatal outcomes.
followup_time: Up to the end of the neonatal period or NICU discharge for fetal outcomes; patients were followed up till labour for Doppler measurements.
